title: "L'Estat du Roy de Navarre et de son party en France", BL Harley MS 1582 ff. 263-264 (DECODE R8505)

steps.what: Checked the catalogue's two records: R8501 (Harley 1582 ff. 71-72) proved to be a Stafford 1586 despatch already read in the sibling target harley1582r8500 from its own f.72r decipherment; only R8505 was open.
Fetched the four full-resolution R8505 images with the DECODE session cookie.

Identified the document from its clear text: the French memoir 'L'Estat du Roy de Navarre & de son party en France', written after 1580, on Navarre's standing, places, gentlemen and alliances. DECODE had no title, no date, no author and gave the language as English.
Searched for the memoir in print and in the Calendars of State Papers Foreign 1583-86, and for a graphic-sign Navarre key in DECODE and Tomokiyo's tables.

Transcribed every cipher run on all four sides (3,630 sign tokens, 56 sign names) against a shared sign chart; lines slope by a full line-height across the page, so runs were followed in overlapping band crops.
IC 0.0398 over 3,630 tokens and Sukhotin's vowel test: consistent with a homophonic alphabet of about 50 signs, not with a syllabary (the commonest sign carries 8.7% of the text).
Homophonic annealing with a 1530-1600 French LM (order 4/5, no spaces) and a unigram-frequency penalty, up to 20 restarts x 400k moves, whole text and page by page.

Control experiment: real French enciphered with a 50-sign homophonic key of the same shape, run through the same solver. It failed too, so the solver was the obstacle; a wrong Sukhotin vowel/consonant constraint and a temperature scale far too small for the log-probability deltas. With both fixed the control solves 100%, and 95.5% with 15% of its signs corrupted.
The corrected annealer on the real text produced French immediately; basin hopping and a word-segmentation objective recovered the whole alphabet.
The recovered key had no sign for m or b, impossible for French: the diagnostic that pointed at the transcription rather than the key.

Second, reading-guided transcription of ff. 263v and 264v against the key: the dot groups are m (controls 'et maintenant', 'l'amitie', 'Monsieur de'), phi is b against f = u ('de beau|caire', 'd'une bonne armee'), E3 is s against E = a, T is u against b = n, eq is f. 513 and 138 sign tokens changed.
Read run by run with the clear-text context (reading.txt); 94.6% of deciphered characters fall inside French words.
Content controls: place-names and persons appear where the clear text leads to them - Beaucaire sur le Rosne, Besiers, Carcassonne, Languedoc, Montmorency, d'Espernon, the prince of Parme, Lisbone.
Constrained emendation of the two sides not re-read from the images, between the proven confusable shape pairs only; reading rises to 95.1% measured.

f. 263v lines 3.18-3.24 re-read on the image and re-decoded sign by sign with key.json to give one continuous run with its clear context (Italian engineer at Lisbon, whose letters came into the writer's hands; the Lorraine marriage 'pour le rejoindre avec [c]este maison ennemie de la chrestienté e[t] particulierement de l'estat d'Angleterre', 'ceu[s] de Guise en Escosse'); one transcription sign corrected (3.23 b -> T), clear words re-read; key unchanged.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 3551 tokens, 57 types, fr-1600-letters order 4: reading -2.265 per letter; random keys -4.815 (z 7.4); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.082 (mean -3.101, z 59.1); annealer on the real text -2.352. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): final/f1-f4.txt (the transcription the reading uses) and reading.txt; key key.json / key_letters.txt with the sign chart signs.md

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). reading.txt read line by line: the cipher stretches are word fragments strung together with [#] holes ('E a nouueau T impos du [#81] ou [#] eam ange ries'), some lines almost pure noise; only the clear French around them reads. docs/_check_reading.py: 84 of 185 sentences clean, the clean ones mostly clear text. Relabelled decoded, not read; class read -> not read, method key recovered from ciphertext-only -> not solved (key work kept as a part); fraction_read 0.951 -> 0.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.265; polyphony 0.0; 95 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.352

outcome.method_basis: The homophonic sign alphabet rebuilt by annealing against a 1530-1600 French model (key recovered from ciphertext-only, recorded under parts) decodes the cipher stretches into French word fragments with holes in most lines; no cipher clause reads as a sentence.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: the one document does not build sentences, so nothing counts as read (0). Withdrawn as a reading figure: 0.951, the share of deciphered characters inside vocabulary words under Viterbi segmentation (final/f1..f4.txt with key.json, evalct.py), which a segmenter reaches on strings of short real words; it measured characters, not sentences.

gaps.detail: names; 14 tokens, nothing in the text fixes them
faint ink and shapes ambiguous within a family; ff. 263r and 264r would gain most from the sign-by-sign re-reading the two versos got

outcome.notes: The cipher was broken here from the ciphertext alone. ff. 263v and 264v were re-read sign by sign against the recovered key; ff. 263r and 264r keep the first transcription corrected by a constrained pass that swaps a token only between shapes the second reading proved confusable and only where the word model gains clearly - 77 tokens, 2% of the text, all logged in emendations_all.txt.

texts.label: R8505, "L'Estat du Roy de Navarre et de son party en France" (Harley MS 1582 ff. 263-264)
texts.summary: A French political memoir, written after 1580, surveying Henri de Navarre as a political asset for an outside reader: his two 'qualitez' (first prince of the blood, chief of the reformed churches), the places and garrisons he holds in Guyenne, Languedoc, Dauphiné and Provence, his following, his alliances and the marriage question; it belongs with Navarre's embassies to the Protestant powers in the mid-1580s. The cipher carries the sensitive clauses inline in the clear French (d'Espernon, Beaucaire sur le Rosne, Besiers, Carcassonne).
texts.note: Word-split decoder output with [#] holes in most lines: the cipher stretches are strings of French word fragments (f. 263v ll. 3.38-3.41 almost pure noise), so the clauses cannot be built into sentences; the clear French around them carries the gist (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026).

parts.label: R8505 cipher stretches (key rebuilt; text decoded, not read)
parts.basis: annealed homophonic key (key.json) against a 1530-1600 French model after a synthetic control; the decode (reading.txt) gives fragments of French words with holes in most lines. Decoded, not read (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026).

prior.where: none found on the DECODE record, in the volume's other records (R8498-R8506), or in print/calendars
